blocks.title: Compositing, keyframes, render queue
blocks.description: Compositions, keyframes and a render queue — the upstream EffectCraft compositor running inside Astravia, on your own machine, with the project you opened in the workspace.

showcase.assistant_reply: Keys at 0 and 12, preview render queued. Capture is frame 6.

items.title: The real compositor
items.description: The tab runs the official EffectCraft web build byte for byte. Upstream's wasm and JavaScript are not patched; only two thin files of ours are added around them.

items.title: Open and render through the workspace
items.description: Opening uses the file selected in the Explorer, and rendered output is written back through Astravia instead of a downloads folder.

items.title: Ask for a frame
items.description: A capture tool saves a PNG of what the canvas shows right now, so a composition can be checked from the conversation.

items.title: Checked at the frame that matters
items.description: Keys are set on the timeline, the playhead is moved to a specific frame and that frame is captured — motion is reviewed at the moment that decides it.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: About 22 MB of editor files arrive on first open and are reused offline after that — no GPU driver, Node or native app to install.

items.title: Open the EffectCraft tab
items.description: The editor needs a WebGPU adapter. On a machine without one it fails at startup and the tab says so instead of showing a blank frame.

items.title: Select a project, then open it
items.description: File → Open inside the editor takes the file selected in Astravia rather than a system dialog.

items.title: Render, then save through the workspace
items.description: Rendered output travels the same bridge as a save, so it lands where you chose.

blocks.content: This build renders through WebGPU. Without an adapter the editor cannot start, and the panel reports the boot failure — it does not retry in software.
Interface language: the editor itself is English only — upstream ships no other language. The tab shell and this page follow your Astravia language.

It scrubs the timeline, sets keys and presses render, one step at a time. The frame it claims to have changed is captured first, so motion is reported from a picture rather than from the keyframe list.
